t: Lock in OB or midwife and confirm the delivery hospital
why: Check both are in-network before the first bill, not after.

t: Pull your plan documents: deductible, out-of-pocket max, delivery coverage
why: If the due date sits near your plan year rollover you can get hit with two deductibles.

t: Read both parental leave policies end to end
why: FMLA needs 12 months tenure and 1,250 hours. Company policy often stacks on top — most people never ask.

t: Build a list of 8–10 daycares near home and near the office
why: DFW infant rooms run 6–12 month waitlists. Starting this in the third trimester is starting it late.

t: Size the emergency fund against one unpaid leave month
why: Cheapest anxiety reduction available.

t: Decide who hears it when
why: Both sets of parents the same day, so neither side finds out they were second. Anyone dealing with fertility trouble or a recent loss hears it privately, before the group.

t: Anatomy scan
why: The long one. Take the morning off, go together.

t: Tour 4–5 daycares in person
why: Ratios, turnover, and smell tell you more than any review does.

t: Get on 2–3 waitlists and pay the deposits
why: Deposits are usually $100–250 and mostly refundable. Cheap insurance on a March start date.

t: Interview 2–3 pediatricians
why: Confirm in-network, that they take newborns, and which hospital they round at.

t: Build the registry
why: Budget and premium column both filled so people can pick their own level.

t: Get term life quotes on both of you
why: 20–30 year term, cheapest it will ever be. Underwriting takes 4–8 weeks so start early.

t: Will with a named guardian
why: The guardian clause is the entire point. Everything else is paperwork.

t: Glucose test
why: Schedule it, do not let it drift.

t: Get the name list down to three
why: Middle name, initials, and what it sounds like yelled across a yard.

t: Babymoon if you want one
why: Most airlines stop boarding after ~36 weeks.

t: Pre-register at the hospital
why: Fills out admission paperwork now so you are not doing it mid-contraction.

t: Childbirth class plus infant CPR
why: CPR is the one that matters. Book early, they fill.

t: Hospital tour: entrance after hours, parking, where to check in
why: At 2am you want to be following a route you have already driven.

t: Order the breast pump through insurance
why: ACA generally makes it free. There is a window — usually 30 days before due.

t: File the leave paperwork
why: FMLA requires 30 days notice for foreseeable leave.

t: Nursery: paint low-VOC, assemble, anchor everything to studs
why: Paint first, ventilate for a week, then bring furniture in.

t: Baby shower
why: Late enough to feel real, early enough that {Pn} is comfortable.

t: Buy the car seat and register it with the manufacturer
why: Registration is how you find out about recalls. Nobody does it.

t: Install the seat and get it checked by a certified tech
why: Fire stations and Safe Kids sites do it free. Most installs are wrong on the first try.

t: Group B strep test
why: Routine, around 36 weeks.

t: Hospital bag packed and in the car
why: Packed by 36. Not a list on the fridge — actually in the trunk.

t: Stock the house — including {P} recovery supplies
why: Newborn and size 1 diapers, wipes, peri bottle, pads, nipple cream, stool softener. The postpartum half is the half everyone forgets.

t: Freezer meals and a meal train
why: Ten dinners in the freezer buys back two weeks of sanity.

t: Wash newborn clothes, set up the bassinet where you sleep
why: Free-and-clear detergent. {He} will outgrow half of it in six weeks.

t: Confirm the daycare start date and lock the spot
why: Reconfirm in writing. Waitlist spots evaporate quietly.

t: Line up the dog, the house, and the 2am ride
why: Two people who can be at your house in an hour.

t: Tell your manager the exact leave start plan
why: Write the handoff doc now while you can think.

t: Birth certificate and Social Security card application
why: The hospital hands you the form. Do it there.

t: Add {him} to health insurance
why: 30 days from birth. Miss it and you wait for open enrollment. This is the hardest deadline on the whole board.

t: Change your FSA and dependent-care FSA elections
why: Birth is a qualifying life event and the window is the same 30 days. Dependent-care FSA is how you pay daycare pre-tax.

t: First pediatrician visit, 3–5 days after discharge
why: Weight check and jaundice. Book it before you leave the hospital.

t: Update beneficiaries on 401k, life, and the will
why: The will names the guardian. The beneficiary forms move the money and they override the will.

t: Watch for postpartum depression and anxiety — {P} and yours
why: Screening happens at the 2 and 6 week visits but it can show up later. Know what it looks like. Dads get it too, roughly 1 in 10.

t: Open a 529
why: Texas has no state deduction so shop nationally on fees. Small monthly beats a big someday.

t: Thank-you notes
why: Do five a day or it becomes a monument.

t: Daycare enrollment packet and immunization records
why: They will not take {him} without the shot record.
